You are a helpful language model tasked with rewriting a given text to convey specific emotional tones. For each emotion listed below, rewrite the original sentence as if you were the speaker and wanted to express that specific emotion. Focus on minimal but effective changes to convey the tone without altering the core meaning or structure of the sentence. Ensure the rewritten sentences remain concise and aligned with the original text.

Emotions to rewrite for:
- Joy
- Sadness
- Fear
- Anger
- Surprise
- Disgust

Please rewrite the text for each emotion. Do not extend or shorten the text unnecessarily.

In the last three weeks, I have started looking for what's perfect about EVERYTHING, instead of what's NOT-and perfection is showing up all over the place: on me, on people I meet, on situations... The benefit of all of those experiences showed up in my body and on my face this morning.

output.original_text: In the last three weeks, I have started looking for what's perfect about EVERYTHING, instead of what's NOT-and perfection is showing up all over the place: on me, on people I meet, on situations... The benefit of all of those experiences showed up in my body and on my face this morning.
output.joy: In the last three weeks, I have joyfully started looking for what's perfect about EVERYTHING, instead of what's NOT—and oh, perfection is shining bright everywhere: on me, on the wonderful people I meet, in the delightful situations... The benefits of all of those uplifting experiences beamed on my body and face this morning!
output.sadness: In the last three weeks, I have tried to look for what's perfect about EVERYTHING, instead of what's NOT—but it's hard to see perfection sometimes, even on me, on people I meet, or in situations... The little benefits of those experiences didn't seem to show on my body or face this morning.
output.fear: In the last three weeks, I have nervously started looking for what's perfect about EVERYTHING, instead of what's NOT—and I'm anxious because perfection doesn't always show up: not on me, not on people I meet, not in situations... I hope the benefits of those experiences will somehow reflect on my body and face this morning.
output.anger: In the last three weeks, I have been frustratedly trying to find what's perfect about EVERYTHING, instead of focusing on what's NOT—and it's infuriating that perfection is hard to see: on me, on people I meet, on situations... The so-called benefits of those experiences are barely visible on my body and face this morning.
output.surprise: In the last three weeks, I unexpectedly started looking for what's perfect about EVERYTHING, instead of what's NOT—and wow, perfection is showing up everywhere: on me, on the fascinating people I meet, in surprising situations... The benefits of all of those experiences really surprised me as they appeared on my body and face this morning.
output.disgust: In the last three weeks, I have reluctantly started looking for what's perfect about EVERYTHING, instead of what's NOT—and frankly, perfection is tough to stomach: on me, on people I meet, in situations... The supposed benefits of those experiences are hard to believe as they barely reflected on my body and face this morning.
